justification: Changes only the wording of the DCP monitor's alert: a new link may now be named as the likely replacement of a held chapter when it carries a new chapter code and exactly the same title. No database write, no served row and no verdict changes.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-10-25 read-only on production: 138 dcp_chapter_registry rows auto_detected. Penrith row #970 (council comparison table) states the DCP was renumbered from 1 October 2026: D2 Residential Development -> C2, C10 Transport, Access and Parking -> B7. Served row #311 (old D2) still downloads with its stored hash, so the hash check reports unchanged.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: held_match matched on chapter number only (#1430), so a renumbered chapter never matched, and on a page with many new links the alert collapsed to one 'page redesigned' line.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Run over all 138 waiting links against every held chapter: 1 match (Penrith 'C2 Residential Development' -> #311), no false pairs.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Not applicable: pure text matching on labels already stored.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A wrong match only adds 'may replace X' to an alert a person reads; a missed match is the old behaviour. A bare title with no code, a one-word title, or an ambiguous title never matches.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: the renumbered Penrith chapters do not match their held chapter, a bare title matches (#1430), a partial or one-word title matches, an ambiguous title picks one, or the plan-name prefix is not stripped
falsifiable_check.observed_red: YES: 5 hand-made mutants (code guard removed, one-word guard removed, ambiguity taken as first hit, plan prefix kept, fallback removed), each killed. The one-word mutant first survived; the test used a label with no digit and was fixed.

functions.name: renumbered_match
functions.input: a new link's text and the council's held chapters {key: label}
functions.output: the one held key whose title, code removed, equals the link's title; else None
functions.if_none: None text or empty held gives None

functions.name: chapter_title
functions.input: a chapter label as stored in the registry or read from a council page
functions.output: lowercase title words with plan name, chapter code and punctuation removed

break_it.scenario: Two held chapters with different numbers share one title (Part 3 and Part 9 Residential Development)
break_it.what_happens: no match; the link is listed without a guess

break_it.scenario: A bare title 'City West' with no code, beside held 'Chapter 7.3 City West'
break_it.how: the link must carry a chapter code

break_it.scenario: A one-word title like 'E1 Appendices' beside a held 'Part F1 Appendices'
break_it.what_happens: no match; one word is too weak
break_it.how: titles under two words never match

break_it.scenario: A renumbered chapter that was also retitled (D3 Commercial -> C3 Employment uses)
break_it.what_happens: no match; the link is listed as a plain new document, as before
break_it.how: exact title only, by design; the person still sees the link
break_it.repro: held_match('C3 Employment and non-residential uses', held) is None

break_it.scenario: Sol: any non-year number counts as a chapter code, so a numbered non-chapter title could pass the code guard
break_it.what_happens: it still needs an exact title match after one code is removed; '12 Smith Street' vs held 'Part E3 12 Smith Street' gives no match, and a wrong match only adds 'may replace X' to an alert a person reads
break_it.how: verdict: accepted, low impact, advisory text only
break_it.repro: held_match('D3 - 12 Smith Street', {'e3': 'Part E3 - 14 Smith Street'}) is None

break_it.scenario: Sol: a chapter number held twice falls through to title matching
break_it.what_happens: intended: 'Part 4 Dual occupancy' picks the held Part 4 with that exact title; bare 'Part 4' still returns None

post_merge.db_reset: None: no schema or data change.
post_merge.other_repo: None: no other repository depends on this.
post_merge.manual_verify: None on the next run: Penrith's C2 link was first seen 2026-10-23, so it is no longer new and will not be alerted again. The Penrith re-onboarding (C2 replacing #311) is handled separately. The fix applies to the next renumbered chapter on any council page.
